review_notes:
I found nothing in this file that justifies a simp-interface change. I read all 110 lines of TranslationC1.lean. I also searched the whole `lean/` tree for `translateCoordinate` and `HasLocalExtension`: both appear only in this file and nowhere downstream. The file declares no simp lemmas and no simp attributes. The only simp use is the local `simp only [standardEmbedding, translateCoordinate, G, ite_eq_left hji / ite_eq_right hji, SphereTranslation.translate]` in the per-coordinate step at the end of `isC1SelfMap_translateCoordinate` (lines 81–88). It deliberately unfolds the two definitions and picks the `if` branch from the local fact `hji`. That is a closed, terminating rewrite with no competing global rules, and nothing in it could loop.

One could add projection lemmas for `translateCoordinate` (the first component, the `i`-th coordinate and the other coordinates) and mark them `@[simp]`. But there is exactly one unfolding site and no other caller anywhere, so I have no evidence that such lemmas would make any real proof simpler or more robust. Proposing them would amount to annotating an identity just because it looks simple, which the rubric excludes.

`hasLocalExtension_of_contDiff` and `isC1SelfMap_translateCoordinate_of_contDiff` are term-mode wrappers that involve no simp. I also checked `Embedding.lean` for how `standardEmbedding` is used. It has no simp lemmas that would compete with the local unfolding here.

Remaining uncertainty: if later files start using `translateCoordinate`, `@[simp]` projection lemmas may become worthwhile, but there are no such uses at this commit.
